title: Unique identifier linking through student ID
description: The student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to link the submitted assignment data to a specific student across the system or context boundary.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking data to a specific individual through combination analysis.
assumptions: Course and timestamp combinations may not be unique across all students

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified data including student ID, course, and submission timestamp which directly identify the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID is used to identify the student in the system

title: Identifier in submitted data
description: The student ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject included in the submitted assignment data.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier within the educational system

title: Quasi-identifier attributes
description: The combination of course and submission timestamp may serve as quasi-identifiers that can support identification of the data subject when combined with student ID.
assumptions: Course and timestamp may not be unique across all students

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The submission timestamp and student ID can be used to attribute the assignment submission to a specific student, preventing denial of the submission.
assumptions: Timestamp and student ID are recorded and can be used for attribution

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Student ID and course information may be more sensitive than strictly required for the functional goal of assignment submission and grading.
assumptions: Functional requirements may not need full student identification for all purposes

title: Excessive data amount
description: The volume of personal data collected (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) may exceed what is functionally needed for assignment submission.
assumptions: Some data elements may be redundant or not strictly necessary

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their assignment data (including metadata like timestamps) is collected, processed, and stored by the system.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Lack of data subject control preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their personal data is processed, stored, or shared within the grades portal system.
assumptions: Limited options for students to customize data processing preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than actually needed for the functional goal of assignment submission and grading.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires collecting only necessary data

title: Linking through student ID
description: Student ID is a unique identifier transmitted in the data flow that can be used to link data across systems and potentially identify the student.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system context.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking data to specific individuals when combined with external information.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes may be unique or near-unique for certain students.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified data including student ID, course, and file reference when routing submission and grading requests.
assumptions: Student ID is personally identifiable information.

title: Transmission of unique identifier
description: Student ID is transmitted as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject across the data flow from P1 to P2.
assumptions: Student ID uniquely identifies the student within the system.

title: Quasi-identifier in metadata
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference in the data flow metadata can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: These attributes together may uniquely identify a student in certain contexts.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The data flow contains records that can be attributed to specific students, preventing them from denying certain claims about their submissions or grades.
assumptions: The data is logged and can be traced back to the student.

title: Observed communications
description: The data flow between P1 and P2 could be observed by network attackers or unauthorized parties, potentially revealing student submissions and grading information.
assumptions: The communication channel may not be adequately protected.

title: Data propagation to unnecessary services
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may not be strictly needed for all processing activities.
assumptions: P2 may not require all the data elements for its core functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (Assignment & Grading Service) that may be broader than functionally necessary.
assumptions: The set of parties receiving data is known at design time.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission and grading data is being transmitted to and processed by the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data flows.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their personal data is processed and shared with the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanisms exist for data sharing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow may process more personal data than strictly necessary (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) for the functional goal of routing submission and grading requests.
assumptions: Some data elements may be redundant or not essential for the routing function.
uncertainty_note: Assessment depends on whether all data elements are functionally required.

title: Unique identifier linking through student ID
description: The assignment store contains student ID which is a unique identifier that can be used to link all stored assignment data to a specific student, enabling identification and potential profiling of the student's academic activities.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system and accessible to authorized parties.

title: Processing of identified information via student ID
description: The system processes identified data containing student ID, which directly reveals the identity of the data subject (student) and enables direct identification without additional information.
assumptions: Student ID is stored in plaintext or can be easily decrypted/recovered.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in assignment metadata
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission time creates quasi-identifiers that could potentially identify students, especially in smaller courses or when combined with external data sources.
assumptions: Course enrollment data is not sufficiently large to provide anonymity, or external data sources exist that could correlate with this information.

title: Attributable evidence of assignment submission
description: The stored assignment file with student ID and submission time creates evidence that can be used to prevent a student from denying they submitted the assignment, supporting non-repudiation of the submission action.
assumptions: The data is stored in a tamper-evident manner and accessible to authorized parties.

title: Extended data retention beyond functional need
description: Assignment files with student identifiers may be retained longer than functionally necessary for grading purposes, potentially increasing exposure risk and violating storage limitation principles.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists or retention exceeds the academic term duration.

title: Student unawareness of data collection and storage
description: Students may not be fully aware that their assignment submissions, including personal identifiers and submission metadata, are being stored in a centralized assignment store.
assumptions: Privacy notices are not clear or students do not read them carefully.

title: Lack of student control over data processing preferences
description: Students may not have the ability to set preferences regarding how their assignment data is processed, stored, or shared with other services.
assumptions: No consent mechanism or preference settings are provided to students for assignment data processing.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The assignment store may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the grading function, including student ID and submission time which may exceed functional requirements.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this educational system.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Assignment data with personal identifiers may be stored longer than necessary for the functional purpose of grading, potentially violating storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this educational system.

title: Teacher identity linked through login credentials
description: Teacher logs in using unique identifier (username/email) which can be used to link all subsequent data flows and submissions to this specific teacher identity.
assumptions: Login credentials are unique and consistently used across the system

title: Quasi-identifiers in submission queue data
description: The submission queue contains course assignments, student IDs, and submission timestamps that can be combined to identify specific teachers and their teaching patterns.
assumptions: Course assignments and submission patterns are unique enough to identify teachers

title: Processing of identified teacher data
description: The system processes identified teacher information including login credentials, course assignments, and submission review activities.
assumptions: Teacher identity is explicitly stored and processed

title: Teacher identifier in system
description: The system contains unique references to teacher identity through login credentials and user accounts.
assumptions: Teacher accounts are created with unique identifiers

title: Teacher actions attributable through system logs
description: Login events and submission review requests can be attributed to specific teachers through system logs and authentication records.
assumptions: System maintains audit logs of teacher activities

title: Teacher communications observable
description: Teacher's login attempts and submission queue requests are observable communications that could be monitored or logged.
assumptions: Network traffic and application logs capture these interactions

title: Potentially sensitive submission data collected
description: Submission queue data may include student work, grades, or comments that are more sensitive than strictly necessary for the teacher's review function.
assumptions: Submission data contains sensitive academic information

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: The system may analyze or enrich submission data beyond what is needed for the teacher to review and grade submissions.
assumptions: System performs additional processing on submission data

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Submission data may be accessible to administrators, other teachers, or support staff beyond the requesting teacher.
assumptions: Multiple user roles have access to submission data

title: Teacher unaware of data collection scope
description: Teachers may not be fully aware of what personal data is collected, how it is processed, or who has access to it.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be comprehensive or clear

title: Limited teacher control over data processing
description: Teachers may have limited ability to set preferences or control how their review activities and associated data are processed.
assumptions: System lacks granular privacy controls for teachers

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the teacher to review submissions (e.g., collecting metadata beyond what's needed for grading).
assumptions: Data collection exceeds functional requirements

title: Potential lawfulness issues with data processing
description: Processing of student submission data may lack clear lawful basis, particularly if consent mechanisms are unclear or if processing sensitive academic data without proper justification.
assumptions: Legal basis for processing student data may be unclear

title: Student name used as unique identifier for linking
description: Student names in the submission data can be used to uniquely identify and link data to specific students within the school context.
assumptions: Student names are unique identifiers within the school system.

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking students
description: Combination of student name, work content, and submission times can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific students.
assumptions: Multiple attributes together can uniquely identify students.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal processes and displays student names and work content, which are explicitly identified information.
assumptions: Student names are personally identifiable information.

title: Linking through parent-child account identifier
description: Parent account is linked to child account, enabling linking of parent's access to child's educational data through unique identifier association
assumptions: Parent account and child account are linked in the system

title: Quasi-identifier combining parent-child relationship
description: Combination of parent identity and child grades can serve as quasi-identifier to link data across contexts
assumptions: Parent-child relationship is stored and can be used for linking

title: Processing of identified data
description: Grades Portal processes identified data including parent account information and child grades
assumptions: System stores and processes identifiable information about parent and child

title: Identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account contains unique references to parent identity that can be used to identify the data subject
assumptions: Parent account includes unique identifiers like username, email, or account ID

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for the login and grade viewing function
assumptions: Grade data is more sensitive than basic account information

title: Revealing attributes

title: Quasi-identifier combining data

title: Profiling an individual

title: Data type sensitivity

title: Predetermined set of parties

title: Unawareness as data subject

title: Lack of control - preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (grades, feedback, submission history) may be processed than is actually needed for parental notification.

title: Linking through unique student identifiers

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination

title: Profiling an individual through grade data

title: Revealing academic performance attributes
